Communication Protocols

How agents talk to each other: Shared State vs. Message Passing.

1. Shared State Protocol

Used in LangGraph. All agents operate on a Single Global State.

  • Pro: Full context visibility. Agent B sees exactly what Agent A saw.
  • Con: Scalability. Context window fills up quickly if 10 agents dump logs into it.

2. Message Passing Protocol

Agents act like microservices. Agent A sends a compressed message to Agent B.

  • Pro: Context isolation. Agent B starts with a clean slate, only knowing what A told it.
  • Con: Information loss. If A forgets to mention a detail, B won't know it.
sequenceDiagram participant Researcher participant Writer Note over Researcher, Writer: Shared State (Full History) Researcher->>SharedState: "I found X, Y, Z about Aliens" SharedState->>Writer: "(Reads X, Y, Z) 'Ok, I will write the blog'" Note over Researcher, Writer: Message Passing (Compressed) Researcher->>Writer: "Summary: Aliens exist. Write a blog." Writer->>Researcher: "Wait, where exactly? You didn't say."
